---
title: "Quarto"
jupyter: php
---

A `.qmd` with PHP cells needs no Quarto extension and no configuration beyond
naming the kernel. Quarto's Jupyter engine starts the kernel, runs the cells in
order, and puts each cell's output into the document. This page was checked
with Quarto 1.10.18, the version CI tests.

Quarto runs its Jupyter engine in a Python interpreter of its own choosing,
which needs Jupyter in it. `juphyter doctor` reports whether it has, and
[Python interpreters and editors](python.qmd) covers how to choose it.

```yaml
---
title: "Highway mileage"
jupyter: php
---
```

A cell is a fenced block whose info string is `{php}`, holding PHP without an
opening tag:

````markdown
```{{php}}
$mpg = \Phibble\DataFrame::fromCsv('mpg.csv');
$mpg;
```
````

`quarto render report.qmd` writes `report.html` beside the document. `--to`
chooses another format, such as `--to typst` for a PDF.

## Naming the kernel

`jupyter: <name>` is the form to use. Quarto resolves the name against the
installed kernelspecs, so it is the `--name` that `juphyter install` was given.

```yaml
---
jupyter: php85
---
```

Jupyter also writes a fuller block into a notebook, and Quarto accepts it in a
`.qmd`. For juphyter it needs one field more than the three Jupyter writes:

```yaml
---
jupyter:
  kernelspec:
    name: php85
    language: php
    display_name: "PHP 8.5"
    path: /Users/you/Library/Jupyter/kernels/php85
---
```

`path` is the directory holding `kernel.json`, shown here for macOS.
[Installation](install.qmd#where-the-kernel-is-registered) lists the directory
on Linux. Quarto's jupyter engine reads it
when it looks beside a kernelspec for a `quarto_setup_cell`, which it does for
any language it has no built-in support for, and `jupyter: <name>` is the only
form that fills the field in by itself. Without `path` the render fails with
`KeyError: 'path'`. Naming the kernel rather than describing it avoids the whole
question.

## Cell options

Quarto's cell options are comments in the cell's own language, written with a
`|` after the comment marker. Quarto has no `php` entry in its
comment-character table and falls back to `#`, which PHP reads as a line
comment, so `#|` is a Quarto cell option and a PHP comment at once.



The options that matter most in a PHP document:

- `#| echo: false` runs the cell and keeps its source out of the page.
- `#| eval: false` shows the source and does not run it.
- `#| output: false` runs the cell and shows no output.
- `#| error: true` lets the render continue past a cell that throws, and keeps
  the traceback in the output.
- `#| fig-cap: "..."` captions the cell's figure.
- `#| label: fig-mileage` gives the figure a cross-reference.

A captioned plot:

::: {#bbae9f0d .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.php .cell-code}
Plot::of(Datasets::mpg())->aes(x: 'cty', y: 'hwy')->point(opacity: 0.5);
```

<script>/* phiz: renders [data-phiz] elements with vega-embed, and re-renders when their spec changes (Livewire morphs). */
(function () {
  if (window.Phiz) return;
  var views = new WeakMap();
  var dark = window.matchMedia ? window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)') : null;

  function parse(json, fallback) {
    if (!json) return fallback;
    try { return JSON.parse(json); } catch (e) { console.error('phiz: invalid JSON', e); return fallback; }
  }

  function target(el) {
    var view = el.querySelector(':scope > [data-phiz-view]');
    if (!view) {
      view = document.createElement('div');
      view.setAttribute('data-phiz-view', '');
      view.setAttribute('wire:ignore', '');
      el.appendChild(view);
    }
    return view;
  }

  function render(el) {
    var embed = Phiz.embed || window.vegaEmbed;
    if (!embed) { pending = true; return; }
    var json = el.getAttribute('data-phiz');
    var optionsJson = el.getAttribute('data-phiz-options') || '';
    var key = json + '\u0000' + optionsJson + '\u0000' + (dark && dark.matches ? 'dark' : 'light');
    var state = views.get(el);
    if (state && state.key === key) return;
    var spec = parse(json, null);
    if (!spec) return;
    var options = parse(optionsJson, {});
    if (options.theme === 'auto') {
      if (dark && dark.matches) options.theme = 'dark'; else delete options.theme;
    }
    if (state && state.view) state.view.finalize();
    // Each render draws into its own element, so a slow, superseded render cannot replace a newer chart.
    var token = {};
    var holder = document.createElement('div');
    target(el).appendChild(holder);
    views.set(el, { key: key, token: token, view: null });
    Promise.resolve(embed(holder, spec, options)).then(function (result) {
      var current = views.get(el);
      if (!current || current.token !== token) { result.view.finalize(); holder.remove(); return; }
      Array.prototype.slice.call(holder.parentNode.children).forEach(function (child) { if (child !== holder) child.remove(); });
      current.view = result.view;
      el.dispatchEvent(new CustomEvent('phiz:rendered', { detail: { view: result.view }, bubbles: true }));
    }).catch(function (error) {
      var current = views.get(el);
      if (!current || current.token !== token) { holder.remove(); return; }
      console.error('phiz:', error);
      holder.textContent = 'Chart error: ' + error.message;
    });
  }

  function scan(root) {
    if (root.nodeType !== 1) return;
    if (root.hasAttribute('data-phiz')) render(root);
    root.querySelectorAll('[data-phiz]').forEach(render);
  }

  function release(root) {
    if (root.nodeType !== 1) return;
    var nodes = root.hasAttribute('data-phiz') ? [root] : [];
    root.querySelectorAll('[data-phiz]').forEach(function (n) { nodes.push(n); });
    nodes.forEach(function (n) {
      if (n.isConnected) return;
      var state = views.get(n);
      if (state && state.view) state.view.finalize();
      views.delete(n);
    });

  var pending = false;
  var Phiz = window.Phiz = {
    embed: null,
    render: render,
    scan: function () { scan(document.documentElement); },
    view: function (el) { var s = views.get(el); return s ? s.view : null; }
  };

  new MutationObserver(function (mutations) {
    mutations.forEach(function (m) {
      if (m.type === 'attributes') { render(m.target); return; }
      m.addedNodes.forEach(scan);
      m.removedNodes.forEach(release);
    });

  function start() { pending = false; Phiz.scan(); }
  if (document.readyState === 'loading') document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', start); else start();

PHP cells come out syntax-highlighted. Pandoc's PHP syntax definition expects a
`<?php` opening tag, which a notebook cell has no place for, and it highlights
the cell regardless.

Every render prints `Unknown message type: 'comm_open'` once, from ipykernel

absence that leaves ipywidgets unsupported, and the message has no effect on
what is rendered.

## What each format carries

A phiz plot publishes four representations and a phibble data frame publishes
two. Each output format takes one of them. For HTML Quarto prefers
`text/html`, for LaTeX and Typst it prefers `image/svg+xml`, and otherwise it
falls back to `text/plain`.

| Format | A phiz plot | A phibble data frame |
|---|---|---|
| `html` | the interactive chart, drawn by Vega-Lite in the browser | the HTML table, with the dimensions and the type row |
| `typst`, `pdf` | the static SVG, placed as a numbered figure | a typeset table; the dimension note and the truncation footer are dropped |
| `ipynb` | the HTML embed | nothing: see below |

A PDF figure comes from the static SVG, which phiz produces by running the
`vl-convert` binary. Install it from
[vl-convert's releases](https://github.com/vega/vl-convert/releases) and put it
on `PATH`, or point `PHIZ_VL_CONVERT` at it. Without it a plot has no SVG and a
PDF has no figure.

`quarto render --to ipynb` is a conversion of the rendered document rather than
the notebook that was executed. Quarto keeps one representation per output and
reaches `ipynb` through Pandoc's Markdown reader. An HTML `<table>` does not
survive that trip, so the output is dropped, and error outputs are dropped as
well.
This is Quarto's conversion rather than anything about the kernel, and a stock
`python3` kernel loses an `IPython.display.HTML('<table>...')` output in exactly
the same way. Render to HTML or to PDF when a document's tables matter.

## PDF output

Quarto produces a PDF through LaTeX or through Typst, and Typst is the easier
of the two here. Typst ships inside Quarto and places an SVG as it is:

```bash
quarto render report.qmd --to typst
```

The LaTeX route needs one more tool. For LaTeX output Quarto also picks the
SVG, and then has to convert it to a PDF, which it does with `rsvg-convert`
from librsvg. Without that binary `quarto render --to pdf` stops with
`Could not convert a SVG to a PDF for output`. Install librsvg, or render
through Typst.

## The kernel daemon

Quarto can keep a kernel alive between renders, which saves starting PHP and
loading the project's autoloader again. Two conditions have to hold, and for a
PHP kernel today the second one does not:

1. The daemon has to be asked for. Quarto turns it on by default only in an
   interactive session outside CI, and `--execute-daemon <seconds>` or
   `execute: daemon: <seconds>` asks for it explicitly.
2. Quarto only keeps a kernel whose language it can write a setup or a cleanup
   cell for. It looks for `lang/<language>` among its own resources and then
   for a `quarto_setup_cell` or `quarto_cleanup_cell` file beside the
   kernelspec. It ships neither for PHP, and `juphyter install` writes neither,
   so the server exits after one render and the next render starts a new
   kernel.

The practical effect is that each render of a PHP document gets a fresh
session, and nothing of a previous render is in scope. Setting

```yaml
execute:
  daemon: false
```

makes that explicit, and is the setting to reach for if a future release starts
daemonizing PHP kernels and a document turns out to depend on a fresh session.
A document that declares a class or a function is such a document: PHP cannot
redeclare either, so a second render against a kept-alive kernel would fail on
the cell that declares it.

The engine is ready for the daemon whenever Quarto starts using it. It has no
read timeout on its end of the socket, so it waits between requests for as long
as the front end leaves it. A kernel made daemonizable on purpose and then left
idle for three minutes between two renders answered the second one from the same
session. When a kept-alive kernel does end, it takes the PHP engine and the
watchdog process that guards it with it, leaving nothing running.

## Freeze

`freeze` works unchanged, because it is Quarto's own cache of a cell's output
and the kernel is not involved in it.

```yaml
execute:
  freeze: auto
```

With `freeze: auto` a document is executed again only when its source
changes. Quarto stores the output in `_freeze/`, and a project that commits
that directory can be rendered on a machine without PHP or the packages the
cells use.

Quarto looks up a document's kernel by name before it reads the frozen
output, so a kernel with that name has to be registered on the rendering
machine even when no cell runs. [Contributing](development.qmd#documentation)
shows how this repository does that for its own site.

## Projects

In a Quarto project the kernel is named per document, in each document's front
matter. A project with more than three documents to render turns the daemon off
unless `--execute-daemon` was passed on the command line, which for PHP changes
nothing.

Quarto runs the kernel with the document's own directory as its working
directory, and the engine finds the
project to load by walking up from there looking for `vendor/autoload.php`. A
document in a subdirectory of a Composer project therefore sees that project. A
document outside any Composer project sees none, and `JUPHYTER_AUTOLOAD` or an
`autoload` entry in a `juphyter.json` beside the document names one outright.
